title: Static & Media Files
description: Manage CSS, JavaScript, images, and user‑uploaded media.

slides.title: Static Files vs. Media Files 🗂️
slides.content:
**Static files** are part of your application (CSS, JS, images that don't change). **Media files** are user‑uploaded content (profile pictures, blog images).

- Django collects static files from each app's `static/` folder and serves them in development.
- Media files are handled separately, often stored in a `media/` folder and served by the web server in production.

slides.title: Organizing Static Files
slides.content: Inside your app, create a `static` folder, and then a folder named after your app (to avoid conflicts): ``` myapp/ static/ myapp/ css/ style.css js/ script.js images/ logo.png ``` In templates, load the static files using the `{% static %}` tag: ```html {% load static %} ```

quizData.question: Which template tag is used to generate the URL for a static file?
quizData.explanation: `{% static %}` is the correct tag, after loading `{% load static %}` at the top of the template.

slides.title: Media Files (User Uploads) 📸
slides.content: For user‑uploaded files, you need to set `MEDIA_URL` and `MEDIA_ROOT` in `settings.py`. In development, you also add a URL pattern to serve media files. **settings.py:** ```python MEDIA_URL = '/media/' MEDIA_ROOT = BASE_DIR / 'media' ``` **In your model:** ```python class Profile(models.Model): avatar = models.ImageField(upload_to='avatars/') ``` **In template:** ```html ```

slides.title: Serving Media in Development
slides.content:
Add this to your project's `urls.py` (only for development):

```python
from django.conf import settings
from django.conf.urls.static import static

urlpatterns = [
    # ... your URLs
]

if settings.DEBUG:
    urlpatterns += static(settings.MEDIA_URL, document_root=settings.MEDIA_ROOT)
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `collectstatic` for deployment

In production, run `python manage.py collectstatic` to gather all static files into a single directory (defined by `STATIC_ROOT`). Then configure your web server (like Nginx) to serve them.
